vm_tools: concierge: do not keep xattrs/fflags in VM exports When exporting VMs, do not attempt to store extended attributes or "fflags" (chattr-style attributes). The files that are being archived should be normal files, aside from having the "encrypted" chattr flag set, which can't be preserved in an archive anyway. When libarchive adds files with these flags to a PAX-style tar file, it creates extra sections that GNU tar doesn't understand, which results in confusing error messages when extracting the tarball. Disable them to avoid adding the extra sections when using libarchive's "restricted pax" format so that the resulting tar file is cleanly extract-able with GNU tar and other tar implementations. UPSTREAM: build_bug.h: remove negative-array fallback for BUILD_BUG_ON() The kernel can only be compiled with an optimization option (-O2, -Os, or the currently proposed -Og). Hence, __OPTIMIZE__ is always defined in the kernel source. The fallback for the -O0 case is just hypothetical and pointless. Moreover, commit 0bb95f80a38f ("Makefile: Globally enable VLA warning") enabled -Wvla warning. The use of variable length arrays is banned. tpm_softclear_utils: implement TPM 2.0 soft-clear Depending on the TPM state, gets the lockout password from tpm_manager local data or uses the default lockout password to clear the owner and endorsement hierarchies of the TPM. BUG=b:134989277 TEST=unit tests; tested on a soraka for the following cases: 1. TPM is fully owned, run `tpm_softclear` to soft-clear TPM, run `tpm_manager_client status` to make sure it becomes unowned, clear tpm_manager local data, restart trunksd and tpm_managerd, run `tpm_manager_client take_ownership` and `tpm_manager_client status` to make sure the ownership can be re-taken. Repeat the process to do stress tests. 2. Similar to 1 but TPM is instead pre-owned w/o local data on disk. Make sure tpm_softclear works correctly. 3. Similar to 2, TPM is pre-owned with stale local data on disk. Make sure tpm_softclear uses the default lockout password to clear the TPM. 4. Repeat 3 and 4 with TPM in the unowned state and make sure everything works.
